summary: A 1952 L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base on Clarke Mountain, Clearwater National Forest. Abandoned, hike-in, and last recorded in poor shape in 2003.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base; a D-6 cupola cabin from the 1920s stood first
facts.status_note: Abandoned and heavily vandalized. The 2003 register visit found the base collapsing and the catwalk unsound.

access.note: Hike-in on National Forest land. No closure notice found in the sources. Structure described as unsafe at last report.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in only. A 2003 visitor walked an old trail from the Bungalow Ranger Station site, which is open to motorcycles. Another route from Elk Mountain is an ATV trail.

events.note: L-4 cab built atop a 10-foot concrete base
Register visit report dated July 12, 2003: base collapsing, catwalk unsound on two sides, sign asks for restoration help, not staffed
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, June 1, 2004

corrections.why: 1952 is the year the L-4 cab was built. The sources say the tower is abandoned but do not date the abandonment.

corrections.proposed: remove; no total tower height in the sources
corrections.why: The 10-foot figure is the concrete base under the cab, not the height of the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 5,208 ft (1,587 m). firelookout.com and the Forest Service list give 5285 ft. The brief's 1587.4 m comes from the register. Elevation is not in the facts block.

sources.title: Clearwater National Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Clearwater National Forest

notes_for_editor: Current condition rests on a 2003 register visit and a 2016 Forest Service list. No newer visit report was found, so check the site before any public claim about its state today. The 1920s cupola has no exact year. The Jimmy Clarke death comes from a hobbyist site citing a book and is included with attribution only.
